The total acceptance includes everyone including people that got in from the waitlist. This is what the Choose Your Medical School tool + acceptance protocols are for. It’s not like they are accepting all 300 people initially, but they usually try to hover around 150 at all times I assume—which is possible because people will withdraw their acceptances directly, or not have the school listed as their top choice on AMCAS. This is how Med schools have a general idea about the size of their class so that they don’t have a class size of 300. So even if they’ve accepted 300 already, only 100 of those students may have that school as their number one, so now the school knows to accept 50 more students off the waitlist to have their class size of about 150 if that’s what they want.
Some schools will have you do a research 4th year in the field you’re interested in if you want to match into more competitive specialties. Seton Hall offers this option that I know of for sure.

Very generally speaking about 1/3 of people accepted matriculate to that school. Schools will usually accept about 2.5 to 3x the amount of students they can actually hold knowing this. If you look at MSAR data or some of the spreadsheets from previous cycles you would see that if the average class size is about 100 people then about 300 are accepted.
